$comment: Declared unreachable surfaces, with a WRITTEN REASON for each. Enforced by
tools/check_reachability.py (CI job 'Reachability - nothing implemented-and-uncalled').
Unreachable is sometimes exactly correct: a capability-denied command MUST have no caller,
and a superseded sibling legitimately outlives its last call site. What hides a defect is
unreachable-AND-undeclared - the state in which nobody can tell which of those it is. So
this file is the point of the gate, not an escape hatch from it: every entry costs a
sentence that a reviewer can disagree with, and 'unreachable, no reason given' is refused
by the gate itself (see MIN_REASON_CHARS / PLACEHOLDER_REASONS).
Adding an entry is a claim. If the command later gains a real caller, the gate turns RED
and asks you to DELETE the entry - deliberately, so an exception cannot silently outlive
the condition it described.
`rust_symbols` covers apps/desktop/src-tauri/** the same way `engine_symbols` covers the
python engine. It needs `module` as well as `defined_in`, because a Rust caller must NAME
the symbol (`module::name(`): a bare-name scan would count any unrelated function of the
same name as a caller, and names like `create_schema` / `resolve` / `sweep` are shared by
half a dozen sibling modules in brops-core. rustc never warns about an uncalled `pub fn`
in a library crate, which is why this whole class was invisible here until 2026-08-09.
`rust_symbols` holds SIX entries as of 2026-08-12, in three groups, and the distinction between
them is the point. [RETRACTED 2026-09-20: the TWO below were DELETED, see above] TWO are the ai-side halves of the 4.10(f) desktop pull that are still unreached
(governed_pull_output, governed_turn_output_read). THREE are
the §4.10(g) submit-frame writer (governed_prepare::prepare_governed_turn_v1b,
::resolve_governed_generation_config_v1b, governed_submit::governed_turn_submit_prepared) - built,
tested, and deliberately not wired, because wiring it would move the shipped broker off its
fail-closed executor. And ONE, `governed_output_pull::pull_output`, is now must_have_caller rather
than declared_unreachable: on 2026-08-12 the live §4.10(f) pull driver
(apps/desktop/src-tauri/core/src/bin/ladder_output_pull.rs) gave it a real named caller, and this
gate's own message says to flip rather than excuse. That caller is a CI PROOF, not a product path;
the gate cannot tell those apart, so the entry says so in prose and the two production blockers it
used to record are written there rather than deleted with it.
TWO entries were DELETED in that same change - governed_bridge_result::parse and ::check_echoes -
because the pull driver calls both and NEITHER call is one this gate can see: `parse` is reached as
the inherent `BridgeTurnResult::parse(` and `check_echoes` as the method `.check_echoes(`, while the
gate matches `module::name(`. They could not be flipped to must_have_caller (that would go RED on a
caller that exists), and leaving them declared_unreachable would have been a declaration that had
become false while the gate stayed green. That is the same hand-deletion, for the same blind spot,
as `parse_frame` earlier the same day - and it is worth restating that a stale declared_unreachable
on live code is the one failure this file cannot be trusted to catch.
2026-08-12, later the same day: the bridge SPAWN moved from apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/ai.rs into
apps/desktop/src-tauri/core/src/governed_sidecar.rs, together with the trust environment it applies
(core/src/engine_trust.rs). None of the entries below changed expectation as a result. Two things
about this gate are worth recording. First, the new seam is reached as an INHERENT associated call
- `GovernedSidecar::as_calling_principal(` from ai.rs and `GovernedSidecar::as_distinct_principal(`
from broker/src/main.rs (it was a single `GovernedSidecar::new(` until 2026-08-12, when the 2.6
principal became a constructor-level choice) - together with `.round_trip(`, the blind spot named
below - so if any of them were
ever declared here, the declaration could go stale without turning the gate red. Second,
`SubmitTransport for GovernedSidecar` is a trait impl with no constructor of its own; a trait impl
cannot be expressed in `rust_symbols` at all, so [RETRACTED 2026-09-20] the fact that it is reachable only through
governed_turn_submit_prepared (which has no caller) is recorded in that entry's prose rather than
enforced here. Neither is a hole this change opened; both are the gate's stated limits, restated
where they now apply.
A SIXTH pull-side entry, governed_bridge_result::parse_frame, was DELETED on 2026-08-12 when
governed_turn_submit_prepared gave it a real production caller. That deletion was made by hand rather
than forced by the gate, and the gap is worth naming: the gate matches `module::name(`, and an
inherent associated call reads as `BridgeTurnResult::parse_frame(`, so it would have stayed green on a
declaration that had become false. A stale `declared_unreachable` on live code is the one failure this
file cannot be trusted to catch, which is why an entry costs a sentence somebody has to keep true.
RETRACTED 2026-09-20, by an audit that read this file's prose against the tree. THREE statements
above are HISTORY. First, `rust_symbols holds SIX entries as of 2026-08-12`: it held SEVEN when this
was written and holds FIVE now: credentials::reference_of was added after that sentence,
and `governed_pull_output` / `governed_turn_output_read` were DELETED on 2026-09-20 with the
app-crate §4.10(f) pull they described (T-103). Second, `SubmitTransport for
GovernedSidecar ... is reachable only through governed_turn_submit_prepared (which has no caller)` is HISTORY:
core/src/governed_sidecar.rs:792 implements it and broker/src/ladder_executor.rs:389 calls the
writer, so both halves are on the production path. Third, of pull_output: `That caller is a CI
PROOF, not a product path` - ladder_executor.rs:330 is a production caller.
The warning written twice above - that a stale declared_unreachable on live code is the one failure
this file cannot be trusted to catch - came true in the OTHER direction, which is why it was not
caught. Every `expectation` here was correct on the day of the audit and still is. What rotted was
the REASONS, on four entries at once, in the only part of this file no gate reads. So the gate now
reads it: every reason/note string here AND in config/spec-conformance.json is scanned for an
absence phrase in the same sentence as a symbol the same run derived a production caller for, and
such a sentence is refused unless it is marked RETRACTED or sits after a superseded-wording marker.
That closes the cheap half of the class. The expensive half - prose about something this gate does
not derive callers for at all - is still only as true as the person who last read it.
Reasons: capability-denied | superseded | governed-wall | backend-only | not-yet-wired.
'not-yet-wired' is an honest OPEN gap and must name where it is tracked.
Observed state recorded 2026-08-07 on branch wave/phase-push-1; the gate re-derives it on
every run rather than trusting these notes.

decide_approval.note: The generic approve verb is DENIED to the main window in capabilities/default.json (deny-decide-approval, T-011): approving must require a renderer-independent native confirmation, so a compromised webview cannot approve anything. Having no caller is the ENFORCED state, not an oversight - apps/desktop/src/features/approvalsAuthority.ts names it only as DENIED_DECIDE_COMMAND, a constant that exists so the page can assert it never renders a control for it. The reachable approve path is confirm_approval; the fail-safe path is reject_approval.
decide_approval.observed: 2026-08-07: no invoke; one non-call mention as DENIED_DECIDE_COMMAND in features/approvalsAuthority.ts.

post_message.note: DENIED to the main window in capabilities/default.json (deny-post-message) and command-policy.json (grant deny) since T-153, on the Owner's decision of 2026-10-02 - this entry itself used to recommend it. Having no caller is now the ENFORCED state: this gate refuses the reason 'capability-denied' unless the grant really is deny. Why it had no caller: post_user_message supersedes it for every renderer path (P1-6). post_user_message fixes the role server-side, so the webview cannot choose it, while post_message only VALIDATES the role against WEBVIEW_MESSAGE_ROLES = ["user"]. services/desktop.ts exposes postMessage(), which invokes post_user_message. post_message was therefore the WIDER of the two - it accepts a role and checks it, where the superseding command never lets the webview name one at all. It stays registered so the grant can be reviewed in one place; commands.rs pins the denial in both files (the_two_commands_no_surface_calls_are_denied_to_the_window).
post_message.observed: 2026-10-02: zero occurrences of the string post_message anywhere under apps/desktop/src/**, production or test; the three computed invoke() names there (agentsDispatch DISPATCH_COMMAND, delegationSource DELEGATION_LIST_COMMAND, integrationsProbe PROBE_COMMAND / DECLARE_COMMAND) are constants naming other commands.

reply_in_conversation.note: The non-streaming twin of stream_reply: same context assembly, same one-time-challenge -> governed_turn -> verify_and_record_receipt pipeline, differing only in delivery. Every chat surface uses the streaming sibling (services/desktop.ts streamReply), so the buffered variant has no frontend wrapper. It is kept because the governed pipeline it carries is the same audited one and a non-streaming caller (automation, a headless turn) is a plausible future consumer; until such a caller exists it is unreached by design.
reply_in_conversation.observed: 2026-08-07: zero invocations under apps/desktop/src/**; commands.rs keeps it on the governed path.

set_run_step_status.note: DENIED to the main window in capabilities/default.json (deny-set-run-step-status) and command-policy.json (grant deny) since T-145 wave 2; the reason here said 'superseded' until T-153, which left this gate not holding the declaration to the grant. No surface authors a run-step status directly. Command.tsx drives steps through stream_run_step (the governed execution path, which sets status as a consequence of real work) and advance_run (which moves the run forward transactionally). A renderer that could stamp an arbitrary step status could claim a step succeeded without it having run, which is the exact honesty defect the six-surface work closed, so it is denied rather than merely left uncalled.
set_run_step_status.observed: 2026-08-07: zero invocations under apps/desktop/src/**; add_run_step / advance_run / stream_run_step are the live callers of the run-step repo.

create_decision.note: An OPEN gap, declared rather than dressed up. The Decisions page is a read-only mirror today - it renders list_decisions plus the engine evidence-chain read - and offers no control that records a decision, so create_decision is registered and allow-granted with nothing invoking it. Two honest closures exist: wire a create control on the Decisions page, or flip the grant to deny because authoring governance decisions from the webview is not wanted. Until one is chosen this is invokable surface with no user.
create_decision.observed: 2026-08-07: zero invocations under apps/desktop/src/**; grant is allow-create-decision, policy tier L1.

assert_no_bytecode_shadow.reason: The worked example this gate was built around, and it CHANGED STATE while the gate was being written. Residual item O-1 (HIGH) is the canonical 'implemented and nothing calls it': the function exists, is documented, raises ProtectedScopeError for __pycache__/.pyc/.pyo under a digest root - and for the whole life of the repository had zero callers, so a forged .pyc could shadow a digest-verified .py and nothing noticed. It now has real callers on the wall's own path, so the expectation is must_have_caller and the gate protects those call sites: if either is refactored away the gate turns RED rather than the defect silently reopening. NOTE THE LIMIT - this proves the calls EXIST; it does not verify the rest of O-1 closure (hooks running python -B, compileall scoped off digest roots, the stray-.pyc regression test), and O-1's status in docs/PHASE_10_PRODUCTION_ITEMS.md is owned there, not here.
assert_no_bytecode_shadow.observed: 2026-08-07: two call sites in engine/runtime/bro_control_plane.py - line 80 in _bind_workspace (before any binding is loaded) and line 267 in the settlement path (a second process the binding path never covers). Both were UNCOMMITTED working-tree changes by a concurrent agent at the time of this run; the gate re-derives them every run, so a revert turns it RED.

head_anchor_payload.reason: The OUT-OF-PROCESS half of the anchor API. `append` assembles the anchor payload itself and refuses any document that is not a signature over exactly those bytes, via the private `_anchor_payload` this function also wraps. What stays caller-less in this repo is deliberate -- the signature comes from the audit signer, a separate service under its own account that mints its own key (`audit_signer::mint_anchor_key`); no person holds, mints or signs with it (Owner decision #78), and a key the ledger's own writer could reach would prove nothing. So this is an exported API for a party outside the engine, NOT dead code. It gains an in-repo caller only if a signing helper ships inside the engine, which would defeat the point. O-2 ITSELF IS OPEN (docs/PHASE_10_PRODUCTION_ITEMS.md): nothing in the shipped product sets BRO_AUDIT_ANCHOR_SIGNER or BRO_AUDIT_ANCHOR_KEY_ID and no installer registers the signer, so every ledger a shipped install writes is UNANCHORED.
head_anchor_payload.observed: 2026-08-07, after O-2 landed: zero call-shaped references outside bro_audit_log.py. The enforcement now lives in `append` + `verify(keys=...)`, which the gate does not track by name.

attach_head_anchor.reason: The storing half of the same out-of-process API: it verifies a signed anchor against the trusted registry and against the ledger's current chain before storing it. Caller-less in this repo for the same reason as `head_anchor_payload` -- the party holding the signing key (the audit signer service, never a person) is outside the engine by design. Not dead code. It is not what keeps O-2 open either: the CODE half landed when `append` started attaching an anchor and keyed `verify` started requiring one, and O-2 stays OPEN because no shipped install configures anchor custody, so `append` has no signer to ask.
attach_head_anchor.observed: 2026-08-07, after O-2 landed: zero call-shaped references outside bro_audit_log.py.

verify_conductor_session_token.reason: ENFORCED, not excused: this is the one of the five that genuinely has a caller, and the gate now protects that. If the call site is removed or refactored away the gate turns RED, because losing it would silently return conductor identity to a plain environment-variable claim.
verify_conductor_session_token.observed: 2026-08-07: called from engine/runtime/bro_completion.py (authorize_conductor_stop path), which also audit-logs the exemption.

require_conductor_session_token.reason: A policy KEY, not a function, so `defined_in` is null and the flag is 'called' by being read. It is read through the named constant CONDUCTOR_SESSION_POLICY_KEY rather than as a bare literal, so the declaration states that one hop and the gate verifies the binding is real before following it - an undeclared indirection would otherwise read as zero readers. IMPORTANT LIMIT, and the reason this entry is worth reading twice: the gate proves the flag is READ by the enforcement path and proves NOTHING about whether it is SET. That second half is outside this gate by construction, and it is now done: engine/.bro/policy.json sets the flag `true`. The `conductor-session` artifact the check then demands is minted by first-launch provisioning with the in-memory operator root, which is destroyed afterwards -- no person holds or mints it (Owner decision #78). Residual item O-3 (MEDIUM) stays OPEN for a different reason: no desktop turn reaches `authorize_conductor_stop` yet.

On that date the flag was absent from engine/.bro/policy.json; re-read 2026-10-01: it is set `true` there.

pull_output.reason: The rev-30 §4.10(f) DESKTOP pull loop: it drives the chunked read, reassembles into a bounded buffer, and applies the §4.6/§7.1 whole-output length+digest gate against the SIGNED envelope (never §4.10(e)'s TRANSPORT-ONLY echo of the same two values). FLIPPED from declared_unreachable to must_have_caller on 2026-08-12, on this gate's own instruction, when `apps/desktop/src-tauri/core/src/bin/ladder_output_pull.rs` gave it a real named caller. Read the flip precisely, because it does NOT say the pull is wired into the product. The caller is a CI PROOF DRIVER: a binary in the crate that owns the loop, built and run only by `engine/ci/live/run_ladder_turn.sh`, which drives one live §4.10(f) pull (and four negative controls) against the real supervisor from the real sidecar principal. It exists in this crate rather than beside the ladder because `pull_output` takes a `ReceiptEnvelope` and has no parameter for the expected length or digest - deliberately, so no caller can aim the gate at the transport echo - so a Python driver would have had to re-implement the loop AND the gate, which is the duplicate-implementation defect this repository has now found seven times. What the flip buys is the thing a declared_unreachable entry could not: this gate now turns RED if that driver is ever deleted, i.e. if the one thing that has ever exercised the loop end to end goes away. PRODUCTION IS STILL UNWIRED, and by the same two named blockers as before. (1) The subprocess spawn on the submit side is an injected seam (`governed_submit::SubmitTransport`) that no production code implements: the tree's one bridge-spawn seam, `governed_sidecar::GovernedSidecar`, is async tokio reached from the renderer-hosting app crate, while the broker binary is synchronous. (2) [RETRACTED 2026-09-20] Nothing calls `governed_turn_submit_prepared`: the broker's one production `GovernedExecutor` (`broker/src/chain_executor.rs::ChainExecutor`) drives the same §4.10(a0)/(a)(b)(c)/(d) hops over DIRECT AF_UNIX and reads the recorder's output off the local filesystem with `std::fs::read(&report_path)` rather than through this egress at all - so even a delivered token would not by itself put the pull on the live path. Reconciling those two architectures is an Architect's call. Neither blocker is expressible as a rust_symbols entry, which is why they are written here. RETRACTED 2026-09-20, by an audit that read this prose against the tree instead of against its own history. THREE sentences above are HISTORY. (a) `The caller is a CI PROOF DRIVER`: `pull_output` has a PRODUCTION caller at apps/desktop/src-tauri/broker/src/ladder_executor.rs:330, inside `LadderChain::pull` (:325), above that file's only `#[cfg(test)]` (:451). (b) `The subprocess spawn on the submit side is an injected seam ... that no production code implements`: `impl SubmitTransport for GovernedSidecar` is at core/src/governed_sidecar.rs:792, built at broker/src/main.rs:515 and passed into the production `LadderChain` at :548. (c) `Nothing calls governed_turn_submit_prepared` is HISTORY: ladder_executor.rs:389 calls it, which is why that entry below is must_have_caller. What this entry lost is the distinction, not the caution: WIRED is not REACHABLE. `build_governed_executor` returns the fail-closed `UpstreamBlockedExecutor` unless `$BROPS_BROKER_CONFIG` resolves (main.rs:268-270), nothing in the product writes that file, and `commands.rs::governed_verification_unconfigured` (:1375) and `governed_turn.rs::connect_broker` (:230) are untouched — so no user can reach a governed turn, and PRODUCTION IS STILL UNREACHABLE is the true sentence the false one was standing in for. This entry's `expectation` was right the whole time; only its prose was wrong, which is why this gate now cross-checks absence phrases against the callers the same run derives.
pull_output.observed: 2026-08-10: zero callers outside governed_output_pull.rs and its #[cfg(test)] module. 2026-08-10 (§4.10(g) sidecar half) and 2026-08-12 (the submit-frame writer): re-derived by the gate in the same run - still zero. 2026-08-12 (the live pull driver): ONE non-test caller, apps/desktop/src-tauri/core/src/bin/ladder_output_pull.rs, which is a CI proof binary and not a product path; the gate cannot tell those apart, so the distinction is stated in `reason` and the entry is must_have_caller rather than deleted.

prepare_governed_turn_v1b.reason: The 4.10(g) v1b single-pass preparation: it validates and caps `system`/`history`, canonicalizes the generation-config OBJECT, computes all three artifact digests ONCE from the bytes that are actually sent, mints the `request_nonce` ONCE, and is the sole source of the pre-store request, the create-pending facts, the submit frame and the final `Expected`. FLIPPED from declared_unreachable to must_have_caller on 2026-08-12 when `broker/src/ladder_executor.rs` called it -- which is the whole substance of that change, because the path it replaced read `system_sha256`/`history_sha256`/`generation_config_sha256` out of `$BROPS_BROKER_CONFIG` and therefore attested the same three digests for every conversation the deployment ever ran. The arithmetic is a test, not a claim: `ladder_executor::tests::the_history_digest_follows_the_conversation_not_the_config` fails if the digest stops moving with the conversation. Same caveat as its sibling entry: a caller is not a reachable user path, and the three fail-closed refusals above it are unchanged.
prepare_governed_turn_v1b.observed: 2026-08-12 (the 4.10(g) broker caller): ONE non-test caller, apps/desktop/src-tauri/broker/src/ladder_executor.rs, re-derived by the gate in the same run that flipped this entry. It is production broker code, not a CI driver and not a test; what still gates it is the DEPLOYMENT, not the code -- see `reason`.

resolve_governed_generation_config_v1b.reason: Resolves the five frozen generation-config fields from the environment into a validated `GovernedGenerationConfig`, which is the only way to obtain one and therefore the only way to reach `prepare_governed_turn_v1b`. FLIPPED from declared_unreachable to must_have_caller on 2026-08-12 with the two entries above, and for the same reason: `broker/src/ladder_executor.rs::LadderChain::run_verified` calls it once per turn so the config the challenge commits to is the config that was validated, rather than a digest copied from somewhere else. It is deliberately re-resolved per turn rather than cached at broker start: the five values are environment-supplied, and a cache would let a turn attest a profile the process no longer runs under.
resolve_governed_generation_config_v1b.observed: 2026-08-12 (the 4.10(g) broker caller): ONE non-test caller, apps/desktop/src-tauri/broker/src/ladder_executor.rs, re-derived by the gate in the same run that flipped this entry. It is production broker code, not a CI driver and not a test; what still gates it is the DEPLOYMENT, not the code -- see `reason`.

governed_turn_submit_prepared.reason: The 4.10(g) submit hop: it asserts the four cross-bindings, writes the `bridge.governed-turn-submit.v1` frame, drives ONE one-shot sidecar through a `SubmitTransport`, and strict-decodes the 4.6 reply. FLIPPED from declared_unreachable to must_have_caller on 2026-08-12, on this gate's own instruction, when `broker/src/ladder_executor.rs::LadderChain::run_verified` gave it a real named caller inside the broker service -- the process 4.10(g)'s Principal binding names. Read the flip precisely. It does NOT say a user can reach a governed turn. The three refusals that hold that line are untouched and byte-identical: `commands.rs::governed_verification_unconfigured` still returns `Some(...)` before the model is invoked -- not unconditionally: it returns `None` once all five of its compile-time inputs are provisioned, and none is -- `connect_broker` still refuses off Linux, and `main.rs::build_governed_executor` still returns the fail-closed `UpstreamBlockedExecutor` whenever `$BROPS_BROKER_CONFIG` is absent, malformed, TCB-violating, missing a manifest, missing a conversation source, or unable to resolve the 2.6 sidecar principal -- which is every shipped install, because nothing in the product writes that config. (Updated 2026-08-12: 'or carrying an unresolved sidecar trust environment' was one of the refusals in that list and is now GONE, deliberately. That refusal was permanent rather than provisional -- the provisioned set's conductor-session token binds agent_id bro-000 / role bro, the CONDUCTOR's identity, and the broker is 0 role #2 -- and it was aimed at the wrong thing: the two frames this transport relays, `bridge.governed-turn-submit.v1` and `bridge.governed-turn-output-read.v1`, reach no reader of the five provisioned variables. The broker now passes `SidecarTrust::RelayFramesOnly`, whose door refuses any request whose own top-level `protocol` is not one of those two, before a process exists. Read the consequence precisely: the broker's ladder was previously unreachable UNCONDITIONALLY, and is now unreachable for the remaining config reasons above, which is every shipped install for the same reason as before. The three refusals named at the top of this entry are still untouched and byte-identical.) The executor it builds is also `ChainExecutor::new`, i.e. no custody resolver, so `persist_committed` refuses the commit even on a fully verified turn. What the flip buys is what a declared_unreachable entry could not: the gate now turns RED if that caller is deleted, i.e. if the shipped broker silently goes back to a path whose three artifact digests come from deployment config rather than from the conversation. RETRACTED 2026-09-20. One sentence above is HISTORY: `The executor it builds is also ChainExecutor::new, i.e. no custody resolver, so persist_committed refuses the commit even on a fully verified turn`. broker/src/main.rs:566 builds `ChainExecutor::with_custody(chain, ...)`, WIRED 2026-09-19 by the Owner's decision recorded in docs/OWNER_ACTION_REQUIRED.md — and main.rs:552-565 records what that does NOT claim: the label a committed row carries is decided by `resolve_trust_state` on the ANCHOR'S PROVENANCE, so a binary pinned to a demonstration anchor still commits `demonstration_custody`, and a turn that verified nothing still commits nothing. Everything else in this entry was re-read against the tree on 2026-09-20 and holds: the three refusals are byte-identical (main.rs:268-270, commands.rs:1375, governed_turn.rs:230), and `every shipped install` is still every shipped install.

It is production broker code, not a CI driver and not a test; what still gates it is the DEPLOYMENT, not the code -- see `reason`.

reference_of.reason: Named `reference_of` and not `resolve`: it resolves nothing, and this gate matches a BARE name as well as `module::name(`, so a generic verb is a false-caller magnet -- `tools/test_check_reachability.py` blacklists `resolve` outright because a deleted ladder once declared one. It returns the stored `auth_ref`, which NAMES where a secret lives on the other side of the trust boundary; it is not a credential and this process holds none, per migration 0022. It has no production caller because the thing that would carry a reference across that boundary -- the transport of a `call` step -- does not exist: repo.rs's Call arm refuses with `call_transport_unimplemented` and uses `credentials::is_bound`, which answers the only question a receipt needs. Shipping the store without the reader would leave the round trip through `normalize_auth_ref` and the schema CHECK -- the part that makes this a reference store rather than a value store -- asserted by nothing. Flip this to must_have_caller in the same commit that adds the transport.
reference_of.observed: 2026-08-31 (§4 rewritten as a reference store): ZERO non-test callers. Exercised by credentials.rs tests only -- binding_with_a_confirmed_grant_stores_the_reference, a_grant_is_consumed_and_does_not_bind_twice, unbinding_needs_no_grant, a_binding_does_not_reach_a_different_build.

accept_prepare.reason: The create-if-absent CAS insert `absent -> ACCEPTED_PREPARED`. It is part of the Rust copy of the section 5 acceptance state machine and outbox, which has no caller outside its own #[cfg(test)] module: the supervisor that runs is Python and its ledger is engine/runtime/governed_supervisor_ledger.py over the same supervisor_ledger.sql. Only create_schema and evidence_floor_cas are reached from other crates. Declared so that the day something calls it this gate says so, instead of a tested library reading as a control in service. Whether to delete the Rust half or to wire a Rust supervisor onto it is a decision about which implementation is the supervisor; it has not been made.

gate_and_start.reason: Runs the step-8a lease-expiry launch gate against the window the ledger persisted and CASes LEASE_READY forward. parse_connect_target.reason: Parses the target of an HTTP CONNECT request for the BUILD agent's egress listener. That listener does not exist: egress_proxy::NOT_IMPLEMENTED says so first, nothing in this tree accepts a CONNECT, and the produced-agent path that IS wired uses EgressGrant::parse_named and EgressGrant::authorize_ref only. The rest of the build-population surface (EgressGrant::parse, ::empty, ::authorize) is equally caller-less but is not declared here, because this gate matches `module::name(` and would never see an inherent call such as `EgressGrant::authorize(` - a declaration that could not turn RED is worse than none. The design says of this module 'Declare it, or CI goes RED'; this is the one function of it the gate can actually watch.

tools/check_prior_art.py.reason: Not a CI gate and deliberately not run as one: it answers a per-SESSION question (has this session recorded what it searched for before creating a new file?) against a receipt that lives in the OS temp directory and never exists on a CI runner. Its caller is .claude/hooks/canonical_law_gate.py at PreToolUse. Running it in CI could only ever pass vacuously, and a check that cannot fail is worse than an absent one because it reads as coverage. Its self-tests DO run, in the ci.yml canonical-law job.

tools/check_merge_ready.py.reason: Not a CI gate and cannot be one: it answers 'may THIS pull request be merged right NOW' by asking GitHub for that pull request's checks, merge state and head, and by comparing PROJECT_STATE.md at that head with today's date. Inside a CI run the question is circular -- the run asking it is one of the checks it would wait for, so it could only ever say 'pending'. Its caller is .claude/hooks/canonical_law_gate.py at PreToolUse, before every `gh pr merge` a session types (T-150). What CI holds instead is the consequence it prevents: check_coordination.py goes RED on `main` when the merge it should have stopped lands. That is true of the DATE rule only. The audit rule added in T-154 (engine security code needs a cited Architect audit or an Owner waiver on roadmap G.2) has no such backstop: a merge that bypasses the hook lands unaudited engine code and nothing on `main` goes red. What CI does hold for it is the drift guard -- test_check_merge_ready fails when config/audit-required-paths.json stops accounting for a root of engine/config/protected-control-plane.json. Its self-tests DO run, in the ci.yml canonical-law job.
tools/check_merge_ready.py.observed: 2026-10-02: invoked from .claude/hooks/canonical_law_gate.py (`merge_problem`); self-tests run by ci.yml job canonical-law.

tools/check_push_ready.py.reason: Not a CI gate and deliberately not run as one: it SELECTS and runs two gates CI already runs unconditionally and by path -- check_bundle_budget.py in perf-budget.yml after a fresh build, check_runbook_snippets.py in supply-chain.yml -- and exists only because a session's argument-free gate loop cannot run the first to a verdict without a build. Running the selector in CI would re-run both for no new information.
